records.name: ANNA Crusis Feminist Choir
records.summary: A community choir based in Center City that holds auditions once a year to add new singers. Members rehearse together and sing in the choir, and the site links to tickets for its performances.
records.what_you_do: Sing soprano or alto parts in the choir, rehearse the music, and take part in its concerts.

schedule.text: Auditions are held once a year in Center City. The most recent round was July 25 and 26, 2026. Rehearsal days and times are not on the pages read.

locations.label: Center City, Philadelphia (audition venue not named on the site)

first_step.how: Watch the audition page for the next round, which says applications usually open in April, or join the newsletter to get audition news by email.
first_step.basis: New singers must audition to join, and the way in is only clear from the audition page.

records.notes: The home page heading reads Auditions 2026 with July 25 and 26. The audition page says the 2025 auditions are closed and its text is older, so the home page is treated as the newer evidence. Mailing address is PO Box 42277, Philadelphia, PA 19101. The phone is also printed as 267-825-SING. Rehearsal location and any fees are not published on the pages read. The choir's home page says all SSAA voices are welcome, which this record reads as soprano and alto parts.

records.name: Singing City
records.summary: A Philadelphia choral group that says it has sung together since 1948. It has an adult choir that rehearses weekly from September through May, and a free youth program called Next Generation for young singers.
records.what_you_do: Adults audition for the choir, then rehearse and sing in its concerts. Young singers can join the free weekly youth program.

schedule.text: The adult choir rehearses Tuesday evenings, 7:20 to 9:50 pm, at Friends Center from September through May, with occasional Saturday all-day rehearsals before major concerts. The free youth program, Next Generation, meets weekly at Temple Music Prep. The site gives its start as September 12 with no year or weekday.

first_step.how: Youth: sign up for Next Generation through the Temple link on the site. Adults: send the audition request form linked on the audition page. That page says the 2026 to 2027 season was taking tenor and bass singers.
first_step.basis: Adult auditions are by invitation after a request form, which closes the adult route to walk-ins. The youth program has open registration.

records.notes: The home page calls the choir's season its 78th artistic season and gives 1948 as the start, but its concert names and the youth start carry no years. Status is active because the audition page names the 2026 to 2027 season as current, though no month is written. Adult singers must live within 50 miles of Philadelphia, sight-read music, and sing a prepared solo at audition. Parking rates on the audition page are not admission costs and are not recorded. Mailing address is 1501 Cherry Street.

records.name: CASA of Philadelphia
records.summary: Volunteer advocates for children in the foster care system. Each volunteer stays with a child's case until it closes, gets to know the child, and speaks up for the child's best interests in court and in the community.
records.what_you_do: Get to know a child, attend court dates when asked, and advocate for what that child needs. Volunteers also take ongoing training.

schedule.text: Training is 30 hours: nine 3-hour sessions over five weeks, one in person and one on Zoom each week. After assignment, volunteers average 10 to 15 hours a month, usually for about two years until the case closes. They must be available for court appearances on advance notice. Training months are listed as January, April and October, with no years.

first_step.how: Attend a CASA information session, listed through the group's Eventbrite page, then complete the application you are invited to after it.
first_step.basis: Volunteers need an information session, an application, a background check, references, an interview and 30 hours of training before a case.

records.notes: The 2026 line in the page footer is a copyright notice and was not counted as dated evidence. No dated news or event appears on the pages read, and the Eventbrite organizer page was not read. Info session dates are not given. Whether volunteers must live in a set area is not stated, and court-ordered status is not stated, so neither is recorded.

records.name: Prisoner Visitation and Support
records.summary: A volunteer group that visits people held in federal and military prisons across the United States, a service it says it has provided since 1968. Trained volunteers visit about once a month, keep in brief correspondence, and write a short report after each visit.
records.what_you_do: Become a volunteer visitor and commit to at least two years of visits, or give money to help recruit and train volunteers.

schedule.text: Visitors visit about once a month and write a short report after each visit. Training comes before the first visit. Visits take place at federal and military prisons across the United States.

first_step.how: Read the become a visitor page on the site, then apply. Training comes before the first visit.
first_step.basis: Training comes first and the commitment is at least two years, and the homepage does not describe the sign-up step.

records.notes: The newest evidence is a homepage item dated 2026-10-02 beside a byline, under a headline about not forgetting people in prison. The fetch could not confirm whether it is a news post, so status and confidence are held at medium. The lead note said the group supports families of people in prison. The site describes no family services, so the record does not claim any. Home page statistics show zero placeholders and were not used. The visitor and donation pages are linked but were not read. Phone is as published on the page.

records.name: Witness to Innocence
records.summary: An advocacy group led by people who were cleared of their convictions after time on death row, together with their family members. It campaigns to end the death penalty and helps exonerated people and their families after release.
records.what_you_do: Get email updates, take action on campaign alerts, ask an exoneree to speak to your group, or give to support the work.

first_step.how: Sign up for email updates, or use the Get Involved page to take action or request a speaker.
first_step.basis: Email updates, action alerts and speaker requests are open to anyone, and the site gives a clear route in.

records.notes: The newest dated item is a May 2025 post about a Geneva conference. The fiscal year 2025 impact report has no month. No meetings or events are listed. The page read gives no phone number. No party or candidate links appear, so the group is kept in scope as advocacy.

records.name: CAIR Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of a civil rights group for Muslim communities. It helps people report discrimination, publishes know-your-rights guides, runs a youth leadership program, and shares voter registration information.
records.what_you_do: Join the email or text list, report discrimination through the reporting form, attend seminars and workshops, or give monthly.

first_step.how: Join the email or text list from the website, or sign up for a seminar or webinar when one is announced.
first_step.basis: The lists and seminars are open to anyone, though the events section on the page showed no dates.

records.notes: The site is the Pennsylvania CAIR site, carrying the Philadelphia chapter's contacts. 267-515-6710 is a voicemail line. A text and WhatsApp line, 215-253-3608, is also published. The news includes October 2026 items on local hate incidents. The group also takes public positions on foreign policy and runs letter campaigns, but it is not a party or candidate group, so it is kept in scope. audience.faith is left blank because the group is open to everyone.

records.name: American Friends Service Committee
records.summary: A Quaker peace and service organization with its main office in Philadelphia. It works on peace and justice issues and runs projects across the country and abroad. Its home page lists no Philadelphia-only programs.
records.what_you_do: Take action on current campaigns, sign up for updates, or look at the volunteer and careers pages.

first_step.how: Sign up for AFSC news and actions through the website.
first_step.basis: Sign-ups and actions are open to anyone, but the site lists no Philadelphia volunteer shift, event or open meeting.

records.notes: Listed in the Friends Center tenant directory. Recorded because the office is in Philadelphia and the group recruits nationally. A reviewer may decide it belongs out of scope. The closest available tag for peace and service work is civil_liberties_privacy. The newest evidence is a home page news item updated Oct 3, 2026, about a mutual aid network, which is not a Philadelphia event.

records.name: Frankford Friends School
records.notes: Hidden as out of scope. It is a PreK to grade 8 school that admits students by application and enrollment, which is an institution a family enrolls in rather than a community group a neighbor joins. The school is under the care of Frankford Monthly Meeting, which may be a separate, joinable group (see leads_only). The www school address redirects to this domain. Admissions banners name 2026 and the 2027 to 2028 school year, with no months, and the newest dated news item gives only the year 2025. No tuition figure was read, so no cost is recorded. Phones as published: 215-533-5368 (Frankford campus, 1500 Orthodox St) and 267-525-6571 (Early Childhood Center, 2537 Frankford Ave). No email address appears as readable text.

leads_only.note: Meets at 1500 Orthodox St and oversees Frankford Friends School. The page lists a business meeting on third Sundays and family worship on fifth Sundays, with no clock times. A Meeting for Reflection is named on the school site. Not checked further.
